intro.title: Empathy
paragraphs: Your dream is to become a successful entrepreneur and create a business that brings people together.

You have just entered the Wellness Center of a large multinational company. Here, you will learn about Empathy — the ability to understand what someone else is feeling, even if their experience is different from yours.
Dr. Elena Ruiz, the Wellness Coach, will guide you through various challenges to help you develop emotional perception, careful listening, and compassionate reasoning.

dialogues.intro: Hi (username)! Now, we'll explore empathy, namely, understanding emotions in others, and responding with care.
dialogues.findStones_initial: For this skill, I've hidden meditation stones that contain a message. Start by checking the shelf with meditation objects.
dialogues.findStones_reminder: The meditation stones should be somewhere in the room. Start by checking the shelf with meditation objects.
dialogues.stonesFound: You found the stones! Click on them to read the message, then bring them back to me.
dialogues.stonesReturned: Great, those steps are your foundation. But, before we continue, let me share something important.
dialogues.empathyExplanation1: Empathy is not just 'being nice.' Empathy is the ability to understand what someone else is feeling, even if their experience is different from yours.
dialogues.empathyExplanation2:
There are actually two sides to empathy:
Emotional empathy:  sensing what someone feels through tone, posture, or expressions.
Cognitive empathy:  understanding their perspective and what might be behind their emotions.
dialogues.empathyExplanation3: When both work together, you don't just notice emotions, but you respond in a way that makes the person feel safe and supported. That's what builds strong relationships at work.
dialogues.empathyExplanation4: Alright, let's put these ideas into practice.

matching.title: Match the emotion cue to its meaning

feedback.wrong: Think about how the body expresses emotions. For example, slumped shoulders often signal low energy or sadness.
feedback.allCorrect: Great work! Continue with the next task.

matching.answerOverlay:
After 3 attempts, here's the answer:

Question: Match body language cues with emotional states.

Correct Matches:
• "Avoiding eye contact" → "Feeling unsure or hesitant" - When people feel uncertain, they often look away to avoid direct engagement
• "Talking unusually fast" → "Feeling anxious" - Rapid speech often indicates nervousness or anxiety
• "Shoulders slumped forward" → "Feeling sad or defeated" - Body posture droops when energy is low
• "Long pauses before responding" → "Feeling overwhelmed" - When processing too much, people need more time to respond

Remember: Body language often reveals emotions that words don't express.

feedback.wrong: Empathetic responses never involve being judgmental or ignoring someone.

fillGap.answerOverlay:
After 3 attempts, here's the answer:

Question: When someone is upset, it helps to (___) their feelings, (___) fully, and ask a (___) question to understand better.

Correct Answer:
• First blank: "validate" - Acknowledging someone's feelings shows you understand and support them
• Second blank: "listen" - Give your full attention without interrupting so the person feels heard and respected
• Third blank: "gentle" - Ask a gentle question to show you care and understand what's going on beneath the surface

Complete sentence: "When someone is upset, it helps to validate their feelings, listen fully, and ask a gentle question to understand better."

pattern.title: Emotional pattern reading

scenarios.text: A colleague gives very short responses, avoids eye contact, and keeps fidgeting with their hands.
scenarios.hint: Fidgeting and avoiding eye contact usually reflect internal tension or worry.

scenarios.text: In a team discussion, a colleague speaks slower than usual, responds with a soft voice, and keeps their shoulders lowered.
scenarios.hint: Lowered shoulders and a soft voice usually indicate lowered emotional energy rather than confidence or irritation.

scenarios.text: A coworker talks very quickly, frequently interrupts, and their gestures are rapid and exaggerated.
scenarios.hint: When someone talks too fast or gestures excessively, it often reflects heightened activation — not calmness or indifference.

stones.title: EMPATHY STEPS

steps.label: Notice
steps.text: Pay attention to emotional cues like tone or posture so you can sense how someone might be feeling.

steps.label: Check-in
steps.text: Ask a gentle question to show you care and to understand what's going on beneath the surface.

steps.label: Listen
steps.text: Give your full attention without interrupting so the person feels heard and respected.

steps.label: Validate
steps.text: Acknowledge their feelings to show understanding and help them feel supported.

fabric.title: EMPATHY REFLECTIONS
reflections: People often hide their feelings behind short answers — empathy helps you notice what's unspoken.
You don't have to fix emotions; acknowledging them is already support.
Understanding someone's feelings strengthens trust and cooperation.
